prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: acceptance/transfer→screening/sortation/make-up→Outbound Load Control Desk; excludes airline loading. No explicit modes. Objectives: safety/identity/throughput/cutoffs. Elements/items (recipients unspecified): Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit records acceptance/ID, sends Oversize Exception Ticket; Bag Tag Printer produces durable unique tags/Calibration Witness Tag; Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) maintains flight IDs/destinations/departures/revisions, sends Flight Cutoff Advisory; Transfer Bag Feeder records arrivals, sends Late Transfer Bag Card, holds pending screening/onward confirmation; Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) coordinates equipment/routes, produces Recovery Route Card; Induction Tray Conveyor spaces bags; North Gate Scanner (Kestrel)/South Gate Scanner identify/image/disposition independently; South produces Manual Rescan Receipt; Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) preserves identity/routes/status, sends Chute Occupancy Note; Image Resolution Desk resolves image holds/dispositions; Bag Reconciliation Station compares ID/active record, flags discrepancies/sends Bag Match Query; East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor selected by plan/capacity; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) stages authorized/valid-disposition bags within flight window, reports constrained capacity; Outbound Load Control Desk confirms readiness; Airline Ramp Coordinator coordinates acceptance/sends Carousel Release Slip upon build authorization. Baggage Control System (Velvet) links passenger/flight/ID, validates records/profiles/sort-plan window/current schedules; routes only within handling/screening/timing/capacity limits; unresolved destinations/exceptions→Secondary Inspection Chute. Dispatch time prioritizes; departure time passenger-facing; schedules include airline dispatch targets/connection windows/timestamped changes. Requirements: verify eligibility/size/weight/ID; hold deficiencies/oversize. Induct only valid-record/available-route/ready-equipment; interlocks stop jams/open doors/unready feeds. Record image quality/alarms; incomplete≠clear; pending/alarm/missing-record requires examination. Identity mismatch blocks dependent routes; blocked chutes prohibit release; authorized-only access. Normal return requires identity/outcome/authorization agreement. Stopped/misdirected bags held until location/ID established. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) manages security holds/escalations with airport security personnel. Isolation: secure/notify Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern); coordinates readiness/staffing/recovery with Security Duty Manager/Maintenance Technician; sets congestion

Document units:
S109: Baggage Control System applies cutoff profiles configured for each carrier, flight, and operating condition.
S110: A bag accepted before cutoff retains its assigned flight unless a subsequent schedule or operational change requires reassessment.
S111: When schedule revisions move a departure earlier, Baggage Operations Supervisor reviews affected flights and directs priority adjustments.
S112: Cutoff values account for screening, sortation, make-up, and transfer handling allowances rather than only aircraft departure.
S113: Baggage Control System receives the Flight Cutoff Advisory.
S114: Baggage Control System compares remaining processing time with route-specific handling estimates.
S115: Bags with confirmed screening clearance may proceed to flight-specific sort destinations when capacity is available.
S116: Bags awaiting screening are held from final flight induction even when their scheduled departure is near.
S117: North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner record screening outcomes for inducted bags.
S118: The Image Resolution Desk reviews unresolved images, and final routing remains withheld until disposition is recorded.
S119: A positive threat indication suspends ordinary routing until the authorized security disposition is entered.
S120: Explosives Response Team produces the Custody Seal Log.
S121: When screening disposition is pending, Baggage Control System preserves a recoverable bag-to-flight association rather than releasing the bag to make-up.
S122: Primary Crossbelt Sorter routes eligible bags according to flight assignment and current cutoff priority.
S123: Concourse Zone Controller coordinates induction demand with available conveyor capacity across the operating area.
S124: Induction Tray Conveyor admits bags in priority order, subject to scan confirmation and safe spacing.
S125: East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor receive flight groups according to active allocation rules.
S126: Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit presents bags for outbound loading only after flight grouping and screening status are confirmed.
S127: Outbound Load Control Desk uses planned dispatch time and load-close targets to monitor whether assigned bags can be accepted.
S128: Airline Ramp Coordinator reports changes to loading readiness that could alter the usable cutoff.
S129: Baggage Operations Supervisor may defer lower-priority bags when a flight's remaining processing window is insufficient.
S130: Bags missing the active flight cutoff are held for reassignment or recovery rather than routed into an unavailable departure build.
S131: Make-up allocation begins when the active flight assignment and available build positions are confirmed.
